title: Silla
capsule: Silla (사라) originated as Saro-guk, a chiefdom in the Jinhan confederacy near present-day Gyeongju, with legendary founding attributed to Bak Hyeokgeose in 57 BCE. The state consolidated into a hereditary monarchy under Naemul Maripgan (r. 356–402), with the Kim clan dominating the throne thereafter; Buddhism was adopted as state religion by Beopheung (r. 514–540), and Jinheung (r. 540–576) built a military that absorbed the Gaya confederacy. Allying with Tang China, Silla conquered Baekje in 660 and Goguryeo in 668, then successfully expelled Tang forces in the Silla-Tang War (670–676) to achieve the first unification of the Korean peninsula south of the Taedong River. The date 682 marks the consolidation of central institutions—including the National Confucian Academy (Gukhak)—following that unification.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial expansion of Silla is documented through Korean annals (Samguk Sagi) and Tang Chinese sources, giving good coverage of the unification-era boundaries, though the early confederacy period is largely reconstructed from archaeology and later chronicles.
